previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after being found unresponsive at home with severe back pain, hypotension, and hypoxia. She was intubated in the field due to suspected STEMI and VT. In the hospital, she was diagnosed with cardiogenic shock, hypoxic respiratory failure, and a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli. She required an intra-aortic balloon pump and vasopressors, which were later weaned. Imaging revealed a left atrial appendage thrombus, multifocal pneumonia, and stable spinal compression fractures. She was treated with antibiotics, anticoagulation, and supportive care. Her mental status improved, and she was successfully extubated. Liver and kidney dysfunction resolved. She developed transient nausea and diarrhea, both managed supportively. After stabilization, she was discharged to a rehabilitation facility for deconditioning with plans for close cardiology and transplant team follow-up.

empirically with IV CTX. Her course was completed with 7 days 
total IV antibiotics and the central line through which her 
medications were given was removed prior to discharge.

inattentiveness on exam. She had a CT head to evaluate for

noted a likely metabolic insult, and her ropinirole was held due 
to excess of tardive/akathetic movements. Her mental status 
cleared without further intervention. Her ropinirole will be

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver is subtly very low in attenuation diffusely,

caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  Moderate colonic fecal
loading is seen throughout the colon to the level of the rectum.  There is
colonic diverticulosis without acute diverticulitis.  The appendix is
borderline in diameter, measuring up to 6-7 mm, increased in caliber as
compared to prior studies, although without clear periappendiceal fat
stranding.

is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

bodies are similar to prior.  Compression deformity of the superior endplate
of L5 is also stable.

SOFT TISSUES: Numerous soft tissue densities in the subcutaneous tissue of the
anterior lower abdomen/ pelvis most likely relate to subcutaneous injections.

IMPRESSION:


1. Borderline diameter of the appendix (up to 6-7 mm) which is increased in
size since prior studies, but without appendiceal stranding.  Findings are
nonspecific.  Correlate with clinical concern for acute appendicitis; a very
early/very mild appendicitis is not entirely excluded in the appropriate
clinical setting, but may be within the realm of normal.  Otherwise, no acute
CT findings in the abdomen or pelvis.
2. Trace bilateral pleural effusions with overlying atelectasis.
3. Status post cholecystectomy.  Stable additional incidental findings
including pancreatic and splenic cystic lesions.
